# Get-ZbxMediaType

## SYNOPSIS

Gets the media types that deliver messages.

## SYNTAX

### All (Default)

```
Get-ZbxMediaType [-Limit <int>] [-SortField <string[]>] [-Id <ulong[]>] [-MediaId <ulong[]>] [-User <ZabbixReference<ZabbixUser>[]>] [-SelectActions] [-SelectMessageTemplates] [-SelectUsers] [-Editable] [-InputObject <PSObject>] [-SortOrder <ZabbixSortOrder[]>] [-Search <Hashtable>] [-SearchByAny] [-StartSearch] [-ExcludeSearch] [-SearchWildcardsEnabled] [-CountOutput] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-First <UInt64>] [-Skip <UInt64>] [-IncludeTotalCount] [<CommonParameters>]
```

```

```

## DESCRIPTION

A media type is how Zabbix delivers a message: email, SMS, a script, or a webhook to a chat or ticketing system. The Get-ZbxMediaType cmdlet reads them with mediatype.get: all of them up to -Limit, by name with -Name (* and ? are wildcards), by id with -Id or from the pipeline, or with the whole mediatype.get selection in -Filter. -User narrows the result to the media types of the given users, each a name, an id or a piped object. It writes ZabbixMediaType objects, with their related objects when a -Select switch asks for them, or, with -CountOutput, the number of matches; it needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Get a media type by name

```powershell
Get-ZbxMediaType -Name 'Mail relay'
```

Gets the media type named Mail relay. A * or ? in -Name makes it a search, so -Name 'Mail*' gets every media type whose name starts with Mail.

### Example 2: Get the media types of a user

```powershell
Get-ZbxMediaType -User 'jdoe'
```

Gets the media types of the user jdoe. -User takes a name, an id or an object; a user piped from Get-ZbxUser binds to it by its UserId property.

### Example 3: Search media types with a filter

```powershell
Get-ZbxMediaType -Filter @{ search = @{ name = 'Mail' }; limit = 10 }
```

-Filter takes the whole mediatype.get selection, keyed by the API's field names: here at most ten media types whose name contains Mail.
